chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, he said:

I wrote to a man asking him to ask Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام about a well that is in the house for wudu (ablution), into which drops of urine or blood fall, or something else falls into it, such as droppings or the like: what is it that purifies it so that wudu (ablution) from it for salat (prayer) becomes permissible?
So he عليه السلام wrote in my letter, in his own handwriting: “Buckets are to be drawn from it.”

The proper way regarding this report is that we understand it as referring to when the blood is little, because that is how he asked him. Do you not see that he said, “Drops of blood fall into it,” and from that smallness is understood? And what the report includes of thirty to forty buckets is to be understood as when the blood is abundant; for that reason he paired it with the slaughter of a sheep that fell into the well while gushing blood, and what is customary in that is abundance. But when that is little, as in the slaughter of a chicken or a pigeon or a nosebleed, he permitted that a small number of buckets be drawn from it, and that is detailed and explained in the first report.

key_terms.الدَّمُ: blood, one of the impurities mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well whose purity and usability are being discussed
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing for salat (prayer)
key_terms.دِلَاءٌ: buckets drawn from the well as part of purification
key_terms.قَطَرَاتٌ: small drops, indicating a limited amount of impurity
key_terms.يُطَهِّرُهَا: purifies it, meaning restores ritual purity to the well water
key_terms.يُنْزَحُ: water is drawn out, referring to removing buckets from the well

ai.seo_question: How is a well purified for wudu (ablution) if drops of blood or urine fall into it according to Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling on a well used for wudu (ablution) when small amounts of impurity, such as drops of urine or blood, fall into it. The Imam عليه السلام instructs that buckets should be drawn from it, and the accompanying explanation clarifies that a small number applies to a small amount of blood, while larger quantities apply when the blood is abundant.
